meta.title: Brain Metastases Epilepsy Risk Score
meta.cff_info:
Brain Metastases Epilepsy Risk Score

Wolpert et al., 2020

DOI: 10.1093/neuonc/noz172

Factors and Points

  • Supratentorial Brain Metastases (BM): 4 points
  • Incomplete Resection: 3 points
  • Multiple Surgeries: 1 point

Risk Estimates

Predicted risk of epilepsy after 5 years based on the score:

Score Risk
0 points 0%
1 point 0%
2 points No data
3 points 6.3%
4 points 8.7%
5 points 11.1%
6 points No data
7 points 22.9%
8 points 47.4%

Additional Study Information

Category Details
Population Derivation: 799 patients, Zurich (2004-2014).
Statistical Methods Univariate and multivariate Cox regression models.
Performance Metrics AUC: 0.75 (derivation).
Generalizability Moderate (limited by retrospective design).
Clinical Utility Helps identify high-risk patients for anti-seizure medication (ASM) treatment or potential prophylaxis.

Newer evidence: seizures after radiosurgery (SAFER interim analysis, 2026)

The first prospective study with seizures as its primary endpoint (de Boisanger et al., Clin Oncol 2026, doi:10.1016/j.clon.2026.104222) followed 75 adults treated with stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) at one UK centre in 2022–2023. 8 of 75 (10.7%, 95% CI 4.7–19.9) had a seizure within 12 months; the cumulative incidence with death as a competing risk was also 10.7% (5.0–18.8), and 9.2% (6/65) for new-onset seizures. Of those seizure-free at 6 months, 3 of 52 (5.8%) had a seizure by 12 months, and no first seizure occurred after month 9. 36 of the 75 had died by 12 months.

How it compares. This score gives a 5-year risk: 8.7% for a supratentorial metastasis without incomplete resection or repeat surgery (score 4). SAFER's 12-month figure is already at or above that, although most SAFER patients were not operated on (12% had a previous craniotomy) and the outcome definitions differ.

This is an interim analysis (375 patients planned; final results expected in 3–4 years) and it reports no risk-factor model, so it neither validates nor refutes this calculator. Seizures were not defined in the protocol, and the paper gives the new-onset rate as 9.2% in the results but 8.2% in its conclusion.
meta.authors: Wolpert F, Lareida A, Terziev R, et al.
meta.clinical_utility: Background Current guidelines do not recommend primary prophylactic anti-epileptic drug (AED) therapy for patients with brain metastases (BM). Yet, subgroups of patients at high seizure risk might still benefit from prophylaxis.
meta.outcome: Risk factors for the development of epilepsy in patients with brain metastases

predictors.name: Supratentorial Brain Metastasis
predictors.assess: Brain metastases located in the supratentorial region (above the tentorium cerebelli), which are linked to a higher seizure risk

predictors.name: Incomplete resection
predictors.assess: The presence of residual tumor after surgery, significantly associated with an increased risk of postoperative seizures, compared to gross total resection.

predictors.name: Multiple surgeries
predictors.assess: Undergoing two or more surgeries for brain metastases, which trends toward an increased risk of postoperative seizures.
